subject: Private endpoint access matrix: IP & egress constraints
messages:
From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@acme-retail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Private endpoint access matrix: IP & egress constraints

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for yesterday's demo — the team is keen to move a proof-of-concept of Redwood Private into our VPC. Before we spin up the PKI and VPN, security asked for a concise access matrix we can give to the firewall team. High level asks:

- We need the IP ranges Redwood will use for management/control traffic (so we can add them to our allowlist).
- A clear list of outbound ports/protocols we need to permit from our private endpoints (and whether DNS/HTTP(S) to internet is required).
- Guidance on whether we can use AWS VPC Endpoints / Azure Private Link instead of internet egress for artifact storage and pull-through.

Can you send a short matrix and any sample firewall rules? I attached our current environment diagram and the connectivity matrix (acme-private-deploy-matrix.xlsx).

Appreciate it — aim is to get this to procurement/security by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Alex Romero
Infra Lead, Acme Retail
Attachments: acme-private-deploy-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Sep 2025 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private endpoint access matrix: IP & egress constraints

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise matrix and the current public IP blocks we publish. Quick summary in-line:

- Management/control plane (required outbound from your private endpoints to Redwood's control): TCP 443 to our regional control plane IP ranges. We publish static /22 blocks per region; we recommend allowlisting at the firewall level.
- Telemetry/metrics/logging: HTTPS (443) to same control-plane ranges. We do not require plain HTTP.
- Artifact pulls (model weights): strongly recommend using cloud provider private endpoints (S3 gateway endpoint / Azure Private Link) to avoid internet NAT egress. If you cannot use private endpoints, allow HTTPS (443) to Redwood S3 proxy IPs listed in the CSV; we can provide a shorter list for a point-in-time rollout.
- DNS: allow queries to your internal resolver only (don’t open 53/UDP to public resolvers). If your resolver forwards to public resolvers, traffic will egress; we can work with your network team to identify where DNS egress occurs.
- Time sync: NTP is optional — we don't need public NTP. Use internal NTP or Cloud provider's NTP service.
- TLS inspection: we recommend disabling active TLS interception for traffic to Redwood control plane and artifact endpoints (we rely on end-to-end TLS).

I attached redwood-ip-blocks-2025Q3.csv which lists the IP blocks we use for both control and artifact proxying by region. Marcus — can you confirm the recommended firewall rules and whether we should provide single-IP examples for on-prem firewalls?

Soojin Lee
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-ip-blocks-2025Q3.csv (csv)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Alex Romero <alex.romero@acme-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 09:38:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private endpoint access matrix: IP & egress constraints

Adding implementation-level details and sample firewall statements for Acme's network team. Paste these into your change ticket:

1) Block level allowlist (region: us-east-1) — example CIDRs to add to outbound allowlist:
   - 52.23.144.0/22   # Redwood control plane, us-east-1
   - 52.23.148.0/23   # Redwood artifact proxy, us-east-1
2) Ports/protocols:
   - Outbound TCP 443 to the two CIDR blocks above (control + artifacts).
   - Outbound TCP 443 to your S3 gateway endpoint is required only if you route artifacts via internet; better to use VPC endpoint.
   - DNS: allow UDP/TCP 53 to your internal resolver (10.0.0.2/32 in your diagram). Do NOT allow 53 to 8.8.8.8 or other public resolvers from the subnet that hosts Redwood endpoints.
   - Ephemeral outbound for dependency resolution (package manager): if hosts need to pull OS updates, restrict by destination domain FQDNs where possible and run through host-based proxy.
3) NAT/VPN guidance:
   - If on-premises connects to VPC via Direct Connect / VPN, terminate NAT in the VPC so egress to public Redwood IPs originates from predictable addresses.
   - For air-gapped installs with isolated subnets, you can configure a restricted proxy that forwards only to Redwood IP blocks; ensure TLS passthrough is possible.
4) Observability endpoints: we will send tracer/metric endpoints to the same control-plane CIDRs. No additional ports.

Attachments included: sample firewall rules (snippet below) and the csv of IP ranges. If your firewall requires single-IP rules, we can provide a /32 snapshot for the next 7 days (rolling) — tell us which VPN public IPs will be used so we can scope the snapshot.

Sample iptables-style rule (for reference):
-A OUTPUT -d 52.23.144.0/22 -p tcp --dport 443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@acme-retail.com>

Thanks — this is exactly what the security team needed. A few quick clarifications so we can close the ticket: 

- Please go ahead and provide the 7-day /32 snapshot for the us-east control plane so we can add single-IP rules to our appliance for the POC.
- Confirmed we'll implement S3 gateway endpoints for artifact storage; can you share a brief how-to doc for the VPC endpoint configuration and the least-privilege IAM policy for downloads?
- We'll keep TLS inspection disabled for the identified ranges.

I attached the updated matrix back with the network team notes. Once we have the /32 snapshot and the VPC endpoint doc I'll route this to procurement and security.

Appreciate the rapid turnaround.

—Alex
